findings.reason: When validateCinematicActorShot recursively validates supporting actors, propBindings is wiped to an empty array ([]) while actor.performance still retains actor.performance.props. validatePropBindings (and runtime checks) requires every animated prop to have a corresponding propBinding; passing [] triggers false failures or bypasses validation against the actual model/prop bindings for supporting actors with props. Furthermore, clockSourceShot should be preserved as the original worldShot context so that world prop bindings and envelopes remain visible during nested actor validation.

In the SVG painter pass, propArt replacement uses RegExp('<g id="' + id + '">[\\s\\S]*?</g>') with string replacement, but supporting actor props rendered earlier in the template are self-closing tags ('<g id="${prefix}prop-${prop.id}"></g>'). In HTML/SVG serializers, empty pairs can be matched, but if minified or self-closed (<g id="..."/>), the regex fails to match. More critically, the regex replace function does not match across the entire shot if identical IDs or namespace prefixes collide, and propArt.set(owner.svgId, ...) registers the exact prefix ID, leaving midground/foreground model targets and labels still referencing `#object-${i}` transforms which causes visual duplication when a supporting actor moves a prop.

When computing relationClock for cinematicRelations, supportingBindings checks boundProp(shot,binding).prefix, which is only set for supporting characters. If all bound props are owned by the primary actor, relationClock falls back to result.compiled.frames. However, if a supporting actor and primary actor both own props concurrently, compiledPropFrames evaluates only frames in the map; if relationClock is not passed when only primary bindings exist or when mixed bindings occur, relation center lookups fail or desync from non-lead keyframes.

dispositions.reason: The provided index excerpt has if(validateWorld)validatePropBindings(shot); canonical world bindings/ownership are fully validated once before actor recursion. Recursive per-person checks deliberately do not revalidate stripped world binding lists. validateCamera receives worldShot:clockSourceShot and board, and the recursive call retains clockSourceShot explicitly. dispositions.status: inferences rejected; separate compound-namespace concern addressed
dispositions.reason: Generated supporting placeholders are explicitly paired <g id=...></g> before the painter runs; there is no intervening minifier/self-closing serializer. replace already uses a callback, not model SVG as a replacement string. Bound object-i groups intentionally contain labels/shadow/focus without a second glyph; foreground is a same-source fragment, following own frames. Unique person and prop IDs do not mathematically guarantee unique compound SVG IDs: actor-a plus b-prop-c and actor-a-prop-b plus c both produce actor-a-prop-b-prop-c. Added an explicit namespace-collision guard and declared counterexample callback; did not add a guessed owner or permit ambiguous IDs.

Any supporting binding has a nonempty prefix, so a mixed-primary/supporting scene already builds compiledPropFrames over ALL bindings/owners. When every binding belongs to the same primary, result.compiled.frames is exactly that owner’s clock and contains every prop. No supporting non-lead keyframe is lost in the explicit branch; runtime continuity/motion still needs human-model verification.
